# 油價再推升升息押注，科技反彈支撐風險資產

## 短天期美債承受政策不確定性回升

週二布蘭特原油升破$91，交易員重新計入部分下週聯準會升息機率，美債再度下跌。這次跌勢由短端領頭，2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.26%，30年期只升2個基點至5.13%，曲線由週一趨陡轉為趨平。

石油衝擊是延續，而非另一個全新事件：美國與伊朗交火進入連續第10天，紅海航運威脅又加重荷莫茲周邊的干擾。改變的是投資人認為央行回應的可能性。期貨顯示7月升息機率約25%，仍低於本月稍早約一半的水準，卻高於最近幾天。實質薪資增加、各州勞動市場大致穩定，也沒有顯示需求已弱到難以承受緊縮政策。

股市沒有同樣謹慎。半導體大漲5.21%，Nasdaq 100上漲1.93%，波動率下降，高收益債基金幾乎持平。信用問題仍集中在個別借款人：Aston Martin債權人升高對資產移轉的挑戰，Car-Mart仰賴證券化的融資模式失靈，其他公司則協商減債、擔保或高成本再融資。股市走強可以減輕眼前避險需求，卻無法替這些公司解決資金問題。

## 通膨傳導尚未實現，短端已先重新定價

布蘭特上漲2.87%至$91.78，WTI上漲1.92%至$84.83。攻擊持續、胡塞組織威脅未解，使荷莫茲與紅海同受關注，也延長了燃料、運費向庫存、消費價格及預期傳導的風險。市場反應的是這種可能性，而不是已有新的通膨數據證明傳導已經發生。

交易清淡可能放大波動。利率市場人士指出，10年期突破4.60%附近、2年期站上4.20%，增加了技術性動能。週一SOFR期貨及選擇權交易量，分別只有各自20日平均的74%、54%。

5年期殖利率上升4個基點至4.37%，10年期升3個基點至4.63%，接近約兩個月高點。升幅隨年期增加而縮小，使2s10s收窄2個基點至37個基點，2s30s收窄3個基點至87個基點。過去一週，2年期、5年期、10年期、30年期分別升8、6、5、5個基點；一個月升幅仍隨年期放大，分別為7、14、17、23個基點，即使週二新增壓力更靠近聯準會敏感的短端。

10年期名目殖利率上升，大部分來自實質利率：實質殖利率升2個基點至2.37%，損益兩平通膨率升1個基點至2.26%。5年期實質殖利率升4個基點至2.09%，7年期升3個基點至2.22%，20年期升1個基點至2.71%，30年期則維持2.91%。這與短端領跌的名目曲線一致，而非長端通膨補償突然出現不成比例的增幅。

本地勞動數據也不支持眼前的成長恐慌。第二季1.209億名全職薪資工作者，每週薪資中位數為$1,251，年增4.6%，高於消費價格的3.9%增幅。季調後中位數由第一季$1,233升至$1,258。能源變貴之際，購買力仍在改善，家庭還有部分所得支撐。

6月失業率在8州下降、2州上升，40州及華盛頓特區穩定，全國失業率大致維持4.2%。非農就業在3州顯著增加、1州減少，其餘基本不變。這不是全面加速，卻也沒有呈現足以抵銷能源疑慮的廣泛勞動市場降溫。

極短期資金仍平靜得多。4週券殖利率維持3.70%，52週券則升4個基點至4.07%，顯示政策不確定性已延伸到下一次會議之外。7月仍以不升息較可能，接下來的物價與活動數據，將決定短端重新增加的利率溢價是合理持續，還是已經過頭。

## 債權保障成為個別融資的分界

Aston Martin債權人把對潛在資產擔保融資的疑慮，升高為法律挑戰。持有公司$18.5億等值2029年到期債券多數的集團發函，主張包括智慧財產權在內的擔保品移轉，將違反適用紐約法的文件，並要求公司在48小時內否決這類交易。產品延後、中國需求疲弱、品質問題與美國關稅，早已使公司仰賴4月取得的£5,000萬股東借款。

BlackRock旗下不同部門也站在協商兩側。債券基金參與既有債權人委員會，私人信貸部門HPS則是討論以移轉資產提供新融資的機構之一。這個重疊不代表交易已有定論，也不構成違反義務的證明，但當既有債權人與潛在優先貸款人同屬關聯平台，資訊隔離就格外重要。

America's Car-Mart呈現了更進一步的循環融資失靈。這家次級汽車經銷商在2022至2024年透過資產擔保債籌措約$25億，後來因消費者損失增加而收緊承作。新貸款減少帶動銷售下降，回收款又留在證券化信託內，使補充車輛庫存的現金減少。庫存下降52%，汽車銷售下降27%；一筆倉儲融資未能落實後，公司關閉136家經銷據點中的42家。

Silver Point的5年期$3億貸款，也未能補好缺口。貸款以SOFR加7.50%計息，附帶最多10%股權認股權證與嚴格控制觸發條款。Car-Mart在6月違約，正考慮出售資產或結束營運，可能在破產程序內或程序外進行。新承作縮減，同時削弱了營運及日後重建業務所需的融資能力。

其他協商也取決於同意門檻與擔保品。Victoria的減債約£3億方案，已獲逾75%的2028年債券持有人支持，但仍未達協議式重整所需的90%。持有人可取得面額75%的2031年第二順位債，以及約19%股權。Millikin University延後的$4,900萬債券，則希望加入一處600床公寓的權利以加強保障，但該資產在截至2026年6月的7年間已虧損約$1,000萬。

HelloFresh新發債在正式重整之前就承受市場壓力。其€3.5億首發債券逾10%可供借券，其中幾乎全部已借出，超過歐洲公司債平均5倍。借券成本達200個基點，同業約50個基點，7月1日以面額發行的債券跌至約95。發行僅3週，借券昂貴且使用率高，顯示空方相當積極。

Oaktree指出，約250家借款人的$2,000億債務，殖利率超過15%或價格低於90美分。這是潛在困境債務的估計，而非已經違約的總額；若高利率持續，這些借款人在不得不再融資時尤其脆弱。

AMC則顯示，營運改善能爭取協商空間。德意志銀行提供$4.25億融資，打開更廣泛再融資的可能。季度收入達紀錄$16億之際，票息15%的債券由3月底約94美分漲至逾109，殖利率降至約9.7%。CCC+評等與仍高的融資殖利率，使執行仍仰賴票房現金流持續，但營運復甦已改善公司的談判位置。

主要信用債價格變化小得多。美債殖利率提高，LQD下跌0.28%至106.85；HYG下跌0.04%至79.65，JNK下跌0.05%至95.90。當天企業消息的核心是現金、擔保與控制權如何在個別借款人內部分配，而不是信用資金無差別撤退。

## 海外財政壓力，遇上已受抑制的民間需求

英國財政辯論持續擾動公債。30年期殖利率一度達5月中以來最高後回落，英鎊下跌0.4%、跌破$1.34。約翰・希利出任財政大臣被視為穩定因素，但£8.5億家庭能源減稅計畫，以及先前對提高國防支出的支持，仍需秋季預算交代如何籌資。

原有財政狀態也沒有多少空間。4至6月赤字£576億，比財政監督機構3月預測高£27億。6月借款受惠於通膨連結支付降低，債息成本比去年少£53億。因此，所得稅及增值稅收入增強，同時伴隨一項難以同規模重現的利息利多；服務、投資、福利與利息支出仍超過收入基礎。

歐元區銀行則已把緊縮傳到借款人。第二季企業、房貸與消費授信標準都收緊，地緣政治及能源風險降低了對弱勢信用的容忍。企業貸款需求因庫存、營運資金、投資與再融資而小增，房貸需求卻在信心疲弱、高利率下明顯減少。ECB會議前，調查說明能源通膨風險與信用敏感需求放緩，為何可能把決策者推向不同方向。

日本財政計畫也未定案。14年成長策略要求¥370兆投資，卻尚未解決可能的食品減稅或國防支出增加所需資金。暫停8%食品稅兩年，估計每年耗資約¥5兆。保障日本銀行自主性的措辭，減輕了政治直接限制貨幣政策的疑慮，但刪除長期保留的財政整頓文字，也使發債問題繼續懸而未決。

相較先前配置提案，這次已有實際長債需求證據。日本保險公司6月淨買入¥6,305億、原始年期逾10年的債券，為3年來最大。海外投資人卻在日本銀行6月升息後，賣出2022年12月以來最多的2至5年期政府債。高長債殖利率吸引了負債配置買盤，政策正常化卻繼續壓抑短天期。

即使官員警告，並在4月28日至5月27日投入¥11.73兆干預，日圓仍一度貶至163.24兌$1。較高美債殖利率、油價與財政不確定性持續構成壓力。弱勢日圓提高進口價格，若國內殖利率因此上升，也會改變日本投資人對海外債券的相對評價。

## 部分新興市場融資改善，另一些選擇延後發債

美元指數上升0.19%至101.184、美國實質殖利率提高，EMB仍小漲0.01%至95.38。總體價格穩定之下，評等、發行選擇與本地政策卻有重要變化。

穆迪將阿根廷由Caa1升至B3、展望正向，為不到3個月第三次升評。財政盈餘、出口、能源與礦業投資、融資改善，以及央行上半年購匯逾$100億，支持這項決定。主權利差約400個基點，為8年最窄。評等仍屬深度投機級，但改善可能擴大機構投資資格；2027年選舉前後政策能否延續，仍攸關後續進展。

印尼開始推銷最多CNY70億的3年期、5年期熊貓債，已獲兩年內最高CNY300億授權。2026年已透過非美元幣別籌措約$70億，週四簿記將測試中國境內需求，但背景仍有印尼盾疲弱、經常帳赤字擴大、能源昂貴，以及穆迪、惠譽的負向展望。

Danantara同時尋求較長美元資金。這家主權財富基金委任銀行安排可能的20年期、30年期優先債，6月才以5年期、10年期券籌得$15億，高於原定$10億目標。惠譽給予擬發債BBB，穆迪Baa2。主權幣別多元化與基金延長美元債期限，找的是不同買方，但都仰賴投資人對印尼政策及投資方向的信心。

奈及利亞維持基準利率26.5%，將中東敵對行動列為最大前景風險。本地煉油及石油產品淨出口提供部分保障，6月通膨也在原預期上升下維持15.9%。委員會仍選擇優先維護物價與金融穩定，而非立即減輕國內借款人負擔。

俄羅斯面對更直接的融資價格歧見。財政部取消7月8日標售、隔週又未取得可接受標單後，暫停OFZ發行。7月只賣出RUB100億，季度目標卻達RUB1.5兆；上半年赤字RUB5.7兆，已高於全年預算RUB3.8兆。停止固定利率供給支撐週二本地債指數，但央行暗示從14.25%再降息的空間減少，政府資金仍需轉向其他來源、浮動券或日後發行。

中國方面，香港裁決讓境外債權人多了一條回收路徑。持有約$7.43億武漢當代違約債券的投資人，可追索包含$1.95億優先票據、約$2,860萬其他持有資產，代價是放棄部分其他請求。境內重整對無擔保債權人的現金支付上限為CNY300萬，較大債權放入5年信託。裁決沒有消除損失，但中國5年違約超過$1,000億後，這提供了額外選項。

匈牙利通膨降至1.7%，連續第二個月低於2%至4%容忍區間後，央行降息25個基點至5.75%。9月檢討前仍可能於夏季繼續寬鬆。福林兌歐元下跌0.2%，較前一次降息後下跌1.9%，構成匯率限制；新政府採用歐元的承諾則支持債券。

其他市場，投資人預期財政更緊、政府更親市場，使哥倫比亞本地公債自總統決選後報酬近9.5%，秘魯約2%。更廣泛的套利交易截至前一週今年已賺約18%，為2005年以來最佳同期表現。低隱含波動率有利報酬，卻使部位容易受到下一次油價、關稅或政策衝擊。

巴基斯坦離開全球市場逾4年後，委任銀行安排一般債與伊斯蘭債計畫。2023年接近違約後，IMF與雙邊支持穩定了經濟；委任是重返市場的一步，不等於交易完成或已有成交價格。這些國家說明，基金價格平靜的一天，仍可同時包含信用改善、新融資管道、延後標售與新增法律回收選項。

## 科技、油價與黃金同時上漲

S&P 500上升0.89%至7,509.20，Nasdaq 100上漲1.93%至29,155.18，半導體大漲5.21%，VIX下降8.58%至17.05。油價與殖利率提高，投資人仍買進先前重挫的晶片股，使美債跌勢難以解讀為全面避險。

反彈沒有抹去先前跌幅。半導體一週仍低2.41%，一個月低13.85%，Nasdaq 100一個月下跌4.11%。接下來財報仍須支持AI投資循環背後的支出計畫與估值。股市需求增強可以降低眼前避險買盤，卻未解決更長期融資問題。

美元較強、實質殖利率較高，黃金仍上漲1.87%至$4,085.20。地緣政治避險與先前下跌後的買盤，和科技股需求回升同時存在。油價依然是通膨預期與名目債最清楚的共同壓力，但尚未讓其他資產一致轉為避險。

## 接下來檢驗短端需要多少政策溢價

7月24日6月新屋銷售、7月27日耐久財訂單初值、7月28日美國經濟指標預估報告，接著就是7月28至29日FOMC。這些資料有助於判斷，利率敏感活動是否已弱到抵銷能源衝擊，或者國內韌性仍讓官員有空間更強力回應。政策聲明再釐清聯準會如何權衡已實現通膨，以及借款成本已帶來的抑制。

ECB即將召開兩天會議，先前6月已升息25個基點，最新企業與家庭授信標準也顯示緊縮。會議措辭將顯示能源通膨與房貸需求下降，哪一項受到較大重視。若官員仍暗示稍後可能升息，即使這次維持利率，也不代表辯論結束。

印尼週四熊貓債簿記，以及Danantara長美元債詢價，直接測試兩種資金策略。最終規模、讓步與投資人興趣，將顯示匯率及能源壓力下，幣別多元化與延長期限能否吸引持續需求。條件確定之前，印尼盾、主權殖利率及Danantara流通債，是較近的信心指標。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Oil revives Fed hike bets, while a technology rebound cushions risk assets

## Short Treasuries bear the cost of renewed policy uncertainty

Treasuries fell again on Tuesday as Brent climbed above $91 and traders restored some of the probability of a Fed increase at the following week's meeting. This time the front end led. The 2-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.26%, compared with a 2-basis-point increase in the 30-year to 5.13%, reversing Monday's steepening with a flatter curve.

The oil shock was continuing rather than new: US-Iran strikes entered a tenth consecutive day, while threats to Red Sea shipping compounded the disruption around Hormuz. What changed was the weight investors assigned to a policy response. Futures put July hike odds around 25%, still below the roughly even chance seen earlier in the month, but higher than in recent sessions. Real wages and broadly stable state labor markets offered little evidence that demand was already too weak to withstand restrictive policy.

Equities did not share the bond market's caution. Semiconductors jumped 5.21%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.93% and volatility fell. High-yield funds were nearly flat. Credit difficulties remained concentrated in individual borrowers: Aston Martin creditors escalated their challenge to possible asset transfers, Car-Mart's securitization-dependent funding model was unraveling, and other companies negotiated debt reduction, collateral or costly refinancing. A stronger equity session could soften immediate risk aversion without resolving those financing problems.

## The front end reprices before inflation pass-through is visible

Brent rose 2.87% to $91.78 and WTI gained 1.92% to $84.83. Continued attacks and Houthi threats kept both Hormuz and the Red Sea in focus, extending the risk that fuel and freight costs would reach inventories, consumer prices and expectations. The market was reacting to that possibility, not to a new inflation release showing that the pass-through had already occurred.

Thin trading may have amplified the response. Rates participants pointed to the 10-year moving through the 4.60% area and the 2-year above 4.20% as levels that added technical momentum. Monday's SOFR futures and options activity had run at only 74% and 54% of their respective 20-day averages.

The 5-year yield rose 4 basis points to 4.37%, the 10-year 3 to 4.63%, near its highest level in about two months. The narrowing daily increases along the curve took 2s10s down 2 basis points to 37 and 2s30s down 3 to 87. Over the week, 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields were up 8, 6, 5 and 5 basis points. The monthly increases still became larger with maturity—7, 14, 17 and 23 basis points—even though Tuesday's marginal pressure was concentrated nearer the Fed.

Real yields accounted for most of the 10-year move: the real rate rose 2 basis points to 2.37% and the breakeven 1 to 2.26%. Five-year real yields increased 4 basis points to 2.09%, seven-year yields 3 to 2.22% and 20-year yields 1 to 2.71%; the 30-year was unchanged at 2.91%. The pattern reinforced the front-led nominal selloff rather than indicating a fresh, disproportionate increase in long-end inflation compensation.

Domestic labor releases gave little support to an immediate growth scare. Median weekly earnings for 120.9 million full-time wage and salary workers were $1,251 in the second quarter, 4.6% above a year earlier, compared with a 3.9% consumer-price increase. The seasonally adjusted median rose to $1,258 from $1,233 in the first quarter. Purchasing power was still improving, leaving households with some income support as energy became more expensive.

June unemployment rates fell in eight states, rose in two and were stable in 40 states and the District of Columbia; the national rate was little changed at 4.2%. Payrolls increased significantly in three states, declined in one and were essentially unchanged elsewhere. These were not signs of broad acceleration, but neither did they show widespread labor-market easing that might have offset energy concerns.

Very short funding remained much calmer. The 4-week bill yield was unchanged at 3.70%, while the 52-week rose 4 basis points to 4.07%. The larger adjustment at one year was consistent with policy uncertainty extending beyond the next meeting. With July still more likely to produce a hold than a hike, the next inflation and activity evidence will determine whether the restored front-end premium proves durable or excessive.

## Creditor protection becomes the dividing line

Aston Martin bondholders turned their concern over a possible asset-backed financing into a legal challenge. Holders of a majority of the automaker's $1.85 billion equivalent of 2029 bonds sent a letter arguing that transfers of collateral, including intellectual property, would breach New York-law documents. They gave the company 48 hours to reject the proposed type of transaction. Product delays, weak Chinese demand, quality problems and US tariffs had already left the company reliant on £50 million of shareholder debt provided in April.

The negotiations also placed parts of BlackRock on different sides. Its bond funds participated in the existing creditor committee, while HPS, its private-credit arm, was among firms discussing new financing backed by transferred assets. The overlap did not establish the outcome or a breach of duty, but underscored the importance of information barriers when existing bondholders and prospective senior lenders sit within affiliated platforms.

America's Car-Mart showed a more advanced breakdown in recurring funding. The subprime auto dealer had borrowed roughly $2.5 billion through asset-backed bonds from 2022 through 2024, then tightened underwriting as consumer losses increased. Lower originations reduced sales while collections remained trapped in securitization trusts, leaving less cash to replenish vehicle inventory. Inventory fell 52% and car sales 27%. The company closed 42 of 136 dealerships after a warehouse facility failed to materialize.

A five-year, $300 million Silver Point loan had not repaired the shortfall. Priced at SOFR plus 7.50%, it included warrants for as much as 10% of equity and tight control triggers. Car-Mart defaulted in June and was considering asset sales or a wind-down, either in or outside bankruptcy. Shrinking originations had weakened both operations and the financing capacity needed to rebuild them.

Other negotiations hinged on consent and collateral. Victoria had support from more than 75% of its 2028 noteholders for a plan to reduce debt by about £300 million, but remained short of the 90% threshold for a consensual deal. Holders were offered second-lien 2031 bonds equal to 75% of face value and about 19% of equity. Millikin University's delayed $49 million bond sought additional protection through rights to a 600-bed apartment complex, although the property had lost about $10 million over the seven years through June 2026.

HelloFresh's newly issued debt was under pressure before any formal restructuring. More than 10% of its €350 million debut bond was available to borrow, and nearly all of that supply was on loan—more than five times the European corporate-bond average. Borrowing cost reached 200 basis points versus about 50 for peers, while the July 1 issue fell from par to roughly 95. Expensive, heavily used borrow indicated active short interest only three weeks after issuance.

Oaktree identified about $200 billion of debt across 250 borrowers yielding more than 15% or trading below 90 cents. That was an estimate of the potential distress pool, not debt already in default. Sustained high rates would leave those borrowers particularly exposed when refinancing became unavoidable.

AMC provided a different outcome where improved operations bought room to negotiate. A $425 million Deutsche Bank financing opened a path toward broader refinancing. Debt with a 15% coupon had rallied from about 94 cents in late March to more than 109, reducing its yield to roughly 9.7%, as quarterly revenue reached a record $1.6 billion. The CCC+ rating and still-high funding yield left execution dependent on continued box-office cash flow, but the operating recovery had improved the company's bargaining position.

Broad credit prices moved much less. LQD declined 0.28% to 106.85 as Treasury yields rose, while HYG slipped 0.04% to 79.65 and JNK 0.05% to 95.90. The day's corporate news was about the distribution of cash, collateral and control within particular borrowers, not an indiscriminate withdrawal from credit.

## Fiscal pressure meets private-sector restraint overseas

Britain's fiscal debate continued to unsettle gilts. Thirty-year yields reached their highest since mid-May before easing, while sterling fell 0.4% to below $1.34. The appointment of John Healey as chancellor was seen as stabilizing, but an £850 million household-energy tax-cut plan and earlier support for higher defense spending left the autumn budget to establish how the new government's priorities would be funded.

The starting point offered little room. The April–June deficit was £57.6 billion, £2.7 billion above the fiscal watchdog's March forecast. June borrowing benefited from a £5.3 billion year-on-year decline in debt-interest costs as inflation-linked payments fell. Stronger income-tax and VAT receipts therefore came alongside a favorable interest-payment effect that was unlikely to recur on the same scale. Spending on services, investment, benefits and interest still exceeded the revenue base.

Euro-area banks were already transmitting restraint to borrowers. They tightened corporate, mortgage and consumer-credit standards in the second quarter as geopolitical and energy risks reduced their tolerance for weaker credits. Corporate loan demand rose slightly for inventories, working capital, investment and refinancing; housing-loan demand fell markedly amid weak confidence and high rates. Ahead of the ECB meeting, the survey showed why energy-induced inflation risk and slowing credit-sensitive demand could point policymakers in different directions.

Japan's fiscal plans were also unresolved. A 14-year growth strategy called for ¥370 trillion of investment without settling the funding for a likely food-tax reduction or higher defense spending. Suspending the 8% food levy for two years was estimated to cost about ¥5 trillion annually. Language protecting BOJ autonomy reduced concern about direct political constraints on monetary policy, but removing the longstanding reference to fiscal consolidation left the issuance question open.

There was now actual evidence of long-bond demand, beyond earlier allocation proposals. Japanese insurers bought a net ¥630.5 billion of bonds with original maturities beyond ten years in June, their largest purchase in three years. Overseas investors, by contrast, sold the most 2- to 5-year government notes since December 2022 after the BOJ's June increase. High long yields were drawing liability-driven buyers even as normalization weighed on shorter maturities.

The yen weakened as far as 163.24 per dollar despite official warnings and ¥11.73 trillion of intervention between April 28 and May 27. Higher US yields, oil costs and fiscal uncertainty continued to challenge the currency. A weak yen increases imported-price pressure; a higher domestic yield in response can also change the relative appeal of overseas bonds to Japanese investors.

## EM access improves for some borrowers, while others defer funding

EMB edged up 0.01% to 95.38 despite the dollar index gaining 0.19% to 101.184 and higher US real yields. The stable aggregate concealed consequential changes in ratings, issuance options and local policy.

Moody's upgraded Argentina to B3 from Caa1 with a positive outlook, its third upgrade in less than three months. Fiscal surpluses, exports, energy and mining investment, improved financing access and more than $10 billion of central-bank foreign-currency purchases in the first half supported the decision. Sovereign spreads were near 400 basis points, their tightest in eight years. The rating remained deeply speculative, but the improvement could broaden institutional eligibility; policy continuity through the 2027 election remained important to further progress.

Indonesia began marketing 3- and 5-year panda bonds of up to CNY7 billion under approval for as much as CNY30 billion over two years. It had already raised around $7 billion in non-dollar currencies during 2026. Thursday's bookbuilding would test demand in the Chinese domestic market against rupiah weakness, a wider current-account deficit, expensive energy and negative outlooks from Moody's and Fitch.

Danantara was pursuing longer dollar funding at the same time. The sovereign wealth fund mandated banks for possible 20- and 30-year senior notes after raising $1.5 billion in 5- and 10-year bonds in June, above its initial $1 billion target. Fitch rated the proposed debt BBB and Moody's Baa2. The sovereign's currency diversification and the fund's proposed extension of dollar maturities sought different buyers, but both depended on confidence in Indonesia's policy and investment agenda.

Nigeria held its benchmark at 26.5%, calling Middle East hostilities the largest risk to the outlook. Domestic refining and net petroleum-product exports offered some protection, and June inflation stayed at 15.9% despite expectations of an increase. The committee still prioritized price and financial stability over relief for domestic borrowers.

Russia faced a more immediate disagreement over acceptable funding costs. The Finance Ministry halted OFZ auctions after canceling a July 8 sale and failing to receive acceptable bids the following week. July issuance totaled only RUB10 billion against a RUB1.5 trillion quarterly target, while the first-half deficit reached RUB5.7 trillion, above the full-year RUB3.8 trillion budget. Suspending fixed-rate supply supported the local bond index on Tuesday but left financing to other sources, floating-rate notes or later issuance as the central bank signaled less room to cut from 14.25%.

In China, a Hong Kong ruling gave offshore creditors an additional recovery route. Holders of about $743 million of defaulted Wuhan Dangdai notes could pursue assets including $195 million of senior notes and roughly $28.6 million of other holdings in exchange for waiving parts of other claims. Domestic restructuring capped cash payments to unsecured creditors at CNY3 million, placing larger claims in a five-year trust. The ruling did not eliminate losses, but expanded the options available after more than $100 billion of Chinese defaults over five years.

Hungary cut its benchmark 25 basis points to 5.75% after inflation slowed to 1.7%, below the 2%–4% tolerance band for a second month. Further summer easing remained possible before a September review. The forint fell 0.2% against the euro and was down 1.9% since the previous cut, providing a currency constraint even as the new government's euro-adoption pledge supported bonds.

Elsewhere, Colombian local government debt had returned almost 9.5% since the presidential runoff and Peru's about 2% as investors anticipated tighter fiscal policy and more market-friendly administrations. The broader carry trade had gained roughly 18% through the prior week, its strongest year-to-date result since 2005. Low implied volatility helped those returns but left positions exposed to another oil, tariff or policy shock.

Pakistan appointed banks for bond and sukuk programs after more than four years away from global markets. IMF and bilateral support had stabilized the economy since its 2023 near-default; the mandates were a step toward access, not evidence of a completed transaction or established price. Across these markets, a quiet fund-level session encompassed improving credit standing, new funding channels, postponed auctions and additional legal recovery options.

## Technology rallies alongside oil and gold

The S&P 500 gained 0.89% to 7,509.20, the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.93% to 29,155.18 and semiconductors jumped 5.21%. VIX fell 8.58% to 17.05. Investors bought beaten-down chipmakers despite higher oil and yields, limiting any interpretation of the Treasury selloff as a broad flight from risk.

The rebound did not erase the drawdown. Semiconductors remained 2.41% lower over the week and 13.85% over the month; the Nasdaq 100 was down 4.11% over the month. Upcoming earnings still needed to support the spending plans and valuations behind the AI investment cycle. Stronger equity demand reduced immediate haven buying without settling the longer financing question.

Gold rose 1.87% to $4,085.20 despite a firmer dollar and higher real yields. Geopolitical hedging and buying after earlier losses coexisted with renewed appetite for technology shares. Oil remained the clearest common pressure on inflation expectations and nominal bonds, but it had not yet produced uniform risk aversion across other assets.

## The next data will test how much policy risk the front end needs

June new-home sales on July 24, advance durable-goods orders on July 27 and advance economic indicators on July 28 lead into the July 28–29 FOMC meeting. They will help establish whether rate-sensitive activity is weakening enough to offset the energy shock, or whether domestic resilience leaves room for officials to respond more forcefully. The policy statement will then clarify how the Fed weighs realized inflation against the restraint already imposed by borrowing costs.

The ECB's imminent two-day meeting follows June's quarter-point increase and the latest evidence of tighter corporate and household credit standards. Its language will show whether energy inflation or declining housing-loan demand receives greater weight. Holding rates need not imply the debate is settled if officials continue to signal a later increase.

Indonesia's Thursday panda-bond bookbuilding and Danantara's sounding for long dollar notes offer direct tests of the two funding strategies. Final size, concessions and investor interest will show whether diversification and maturity extension are attracting durable demand despite currency and energy pressures. Until terms are established, the rupiah, sovereign yields and Danantara's existing bonds provide the nearer measures of confidence.
